description: In WebKitGTK 2.52.6 (Even simulator engine) streaming Silero VAD runs at RTF 2.1 (~69 ms per 512-sample session.run) through the app's engines, while Moonshine's large kernels are fine and Node runs the same build fast. ort-env.ts loads the asyncify (native WebGPU) build for every worker, including the CPU-only audio worker. Measure Silero per-call time in WebKitGTK with: asyncify build (current), plain ort-wasm-simd-threaded build, and jsep; isolate JS-side per-call overhead. JSC is also the iOS WebView engine. Output: numbers and a recommendation.

comments.text:
Measured in WebKitGTK 2.52.6 (simulator engine), Silero VAD v6, 250 x 512-sample session.run calls in a dedicated worker, jfk.wav:
- asyncify (app's build) threads=1: median 0.40-0.48 ms/call (RTF 0.013-0.015); threads=4 (what ort-env picks since crossOriginIsolated is true without SAB): 0.56 ms; with a CAM++ session in the same WASM instance: 0.64 ms
- plain ort-wasm-simd-threaded: 0.32 ms (RTF 0.012)
- jsep: 0.60 ms; jspi: unsupported in JSC ('WebAssembly JSPI is not supported')
- App path (LocalEngines -> audio.worker vad.push, 4 s audio): 0.23 s VAD-only, 0.16 s after CAM++ load (RTF ~0.05).
Conclusion: the asyncify build is not a VAD bottleneck; the plain build saves ~0.1 ms/call, not worth a second runtime. The earlier 8.6 s / 4 s reading did not reproduce (machine load avg 4-8 during runs). What is slow in WebKitGTK is session creation: Moonshine Base 34.6 s, CAM++ 3.8-21.7 s (varies with load). Recommendation: keep one ORT build; address load latency (warm at launch 9ij.17, caption speech said while loading 9ij.21) and consider looking at session-creation cost (graph optimization level, fp32 encoder) separately.

title: Measure ORT non-asyncify WASM build for the audio worker in WebKitGTK
